free_tier.stated: Free trial: 60 minutes on one small computer, no sign-up, no card; one hour of credit with full internet also comes with every new account.
free_tier.notes: The anonymous trial is one small computer for 60 minutes in total, counted only while it runs. One trial per device every 30 days and one new trial per internet connection per day. The free computer is kept for 3 days after last use before deletion, and a signed-in account inherits it.

per_object_cap.stated: A small computer has 10 GB of disk and a large one 20 GB; no larger single-disk size is published.

retention.stated: Stopping keeps files, installed software and processes; an idle computer is stopped after an hour, and a trial computer is deleted after 3 days without use. No backup exists and files can be lost if hardware fails.
retention.notes: The 3 days apply to an unused free-trial computer; paid computers are kept until the user deletes them, with no published retention period.

egress.terms: Full internet access on paid computers; the anonymous trial limits internet to code and package sites and AI model APIs. No egress allowance or per-GB price is published.

interface_detail: A CLI with run, exec, stop and auth commands drives the computers; the SDKs and the browser sign-in flow are documented. Incoming connections and hosting a website are not supported.
tooling: workpaper CLI, installed with a shell script, with SDKs for scripts and agents.
chaining: A CLI-driven computer can run agent tasks and keep files across stops; without incoming connections or backups, results must be copied out or kept in git.

limits.value: 60 minutes on one small computer for the anonymous trial; 1,500 small-VM hours a month on Pro
4 running computers per account, shared across small and large sizes
one trial per device every 30 days and one new trial per internet connection per day

limits_note: New Pro sign-ups join a waitlist when the operator is at capacity; paying users run before free trials, and a running free computer may be stopped to make room.
binding_note: The 60-minute anonymous trial runs out first: a single small computer at USD 0.010 an hour would cost USD 0.60 for that hour, before the 4-computer account limit or the waitlist.

identity_cost.detail: The anonymous free trial needs no sign-up and no card: the CLI starts it directly. Paid plans and keeping the computer need an account, created with Google or a 6-digit code sent to email; Pro is paid by subscription or a one-time top-up.

reliability_note: Computers run on privately operated hardware in India with limited capacity and occasional 'no free computers right now' errors; no backups, no uptime guarantee, no GPUs, and no incoming connections.
confidence_note: The rate card, free-trial terms, account limits, sign-in methods and reliability caveats were read from first-party pages today.
